# Weekly Book Topics 50Q - week of 23 Aug 2026 (Sun 23 - Sat 29 Aug)

*Auto-generated for UPSC CSE 2027 prep. Feeds the website's Sectional practice flow. Static book-topic set, not current affairs.*

## Week focus

Basis: this week's **Sunday Sweep (2026-08-23)**, which covers **Sun 23 -> Sat 29 Aug 2026** and explicitly asks for the Book-topics 50Q to be run against the week's Judiciary/Committees Polity block "while the committee compositions are warm." The set is therefore weighted toward that spine, with the rest of the week's static reading covered proportionally:

- **Polity - Parliamentary Committees, Forums & Group** (Laxmikanth Ch 23-25): the week's anchor. PAC / Estimates / CoPU / DRSC compositions and mandates, ad hoc vs standing committees, Parliamentary Forums, Indian Parliamentary Group. **(Q1-10)**
- **Polity - Supreme Court & the Judiciary** (Laxmikanth Ch 26-29): establishment and strength, qualifications, the five jurisdictions, judicial review and basic structure, NJAC, judicial activism and PIL landmarks. **(Q11-20)**
- **Economy - Agriculture I & II** (Vivek Singh Ch 10-11, with NCERT frame): CACP and MSP cost concepts, FRP, FCI/NFSA/PDS, agri-marketing (e-NAM, AIF), irrigation (PMKSY) and crop insurance (PMFBY). Economy is studied from NCERT + Vivek Singh, not Mrunal. **(Q21-29)**
- **Modern History - 1945-47** (Spectrum Ch 24-25) + the thematic chapter on **Constitutional, Administrative and Judicial Developments**: Cabinet Mission, Direct Action Day, Interim Government, Mountbatten Plan, Independence Act, Radcliffe; plus the 1773-1935 constitutional ladder. **(Q30-38)**
- **Geography - Human geography** (NCERT-12 *India: People and Economy* Ch 1-3): population, migration streams and reasons, human development. **(Q39-44)**
- **International Relations - India-China** (F7 IR allocation): the agreement ladder, boundary geography, the Oct 2024 patrolling understanding. **(Q45-48)**
- **Environment - Environmental Pollution** (Shankar IAS Ch 6, pulled forward this week as noted in the Sweep; treated here as a light **revision** block, not a repeat expansion): pollution legislation and the AQI. **(Q49-50)**

**Why these, and no repeats:** the last book-topics sets (02, 09, 11, 16 Aug) closed the Union legislature and executive (Laxmikanth Ch 14-22), Vivek Singh through Ch 7, Spectrum through the INA (Ch 23), and physical geography. This week advances cleanly into the Judiciary, Agriculture, and Partition, with no chapter repeated. Environmental Pollution appeared on 11 Aug, so it is deliberately kept to two revision questions only.

**One verified update:** the Sweep's Supreme Court strength of "34" is now outdated. The **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026** raised the sanctioned strength to **38 (CJI + 37)**; Q12 uses the current figure. The Oct 2024 India-China Depsang-Demchok patrolling understanding (Q48) was web-verified before use.

## How to use

Do all 50 in one **60-minute** timed sitting, no notes, mark and move. Then debrief only the wrong ones and any lucky guesses. Difficulty mix is **15 Easy / 25 Moderate / 10 Hard** - if you drop more than 3 of the Easy set, the compositions haven't set yet and you should re-read the relevant chapter the same evening. Statement-based and matching questions are the exam's real battleground here: for every wrong answer, write in one line *why the wrong statement is wrong*, not just the right option. Come back for a blind re-take on Wednesday.

## Answer key with explanations

**Q1. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - The PAC has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha). Its term is one year and, by convention since 1967, its chairman is from the Opposition. A minister cannot be elected as a member, so statement 2 is wrong.

**Q2. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - The Estimates Committee (constituted 1950) is the largest parliamentary committee with 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has no representation. It cannot question the policy laid down by Parliament - it only suggests economies in administration. Hence statement 3 is wrong.

**Q3. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - The CoPU was created in 1964 on the recommendation of the Krishna Menon Committee. Its membership was raised from the original 15 to 22 (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha). Like other financial committees, ministers cannot be members, so statement 3 is wrong.

**Q4. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - The DRSC system began with 17 committees in 1993 and was restructured to 24 in 2004. Each has 31 members (21 Lok Sabha + 10 Rajya Sabha); 16 function under the Speaker and 8 under the Rajya Sabha Chairman. Their recommendations are advisory (persuasive), not binding, so statement 3 is wrong.

**Q5. Answer: (c)** - *Hard* - PAC is the oldest (1921), Estimates Committee 1950, CoPU 1964, and the DRSC system was introduced in 1993. Correct sequence: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

**Q6. Answer: (b)** - *Moderate* - The PAC works on the audited accounts and the audit reports of the CAG - i.e. after the money has been spent. Because it cannot stop expenditure in advance and acts only afterwards, its role is often criticised as a post-mortem examination.

**Q7. Answer: (d)** - *Easy* - The IPG, formed in 1949, is an autonomous body (not a parliamentary committee). The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is its ex-officio President, and it serves as the Indian national group of the IPU and the main branch of the CPA in India. All three statements are correct.

**Q8. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - Parliamentary Forums were first constituted in 2005 to sensitise members on critical issues (water, youth, population, disaster management, etc.). The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the ex-officio President of the forums located in the Lok Sabha. Both statements are correct.

**Q9. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - Ad hoc committees are appointed for a specific purpose and cease to exist once the task is completed - e.g. Select/Joint Committees on Bills and Joint Parliamentary Committees. The other three are standing committees, which are permanent and constituted periodically.

**Q10. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - The PAC examines the appropriation accounts and the finance accounts of the Union government together with the audit reports of the CAG. It does not deal with budget estimates (Estimates Committee) or demands for grants; examination of public undertakings falls to the CoPU.

**Q11. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - Article 124 provides for the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court. Article 131 deals with original jurisdiction, Article 143 with advisory jurisdiction, and Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs.

**Q12. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - Under Article 124, Parliament fixes the number of judges. The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026 raised the sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 (the Chief Justice of India plus 37 other judges). The earlier figure of 34 dated from the 2019 amendment.

**Q13. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - A distinguished jurist may be appointed (this route has never yet been used), and five years as a High Court judge (or ten years as a High Court advocate) is a qualifying criterion. The Constitution prescribes no minimum age for a Supreme Court judge, so statement 2 is wrong.

**Q14. Answer: (c)** - *Hard* - Article 131 gives the Supreme Court exclusive original jurisdiction over federal disputes (Centre-State, State-State, etc.). However, inter-State water disputes are expressly excluded - Article 262 allows Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of all courts, done through the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956. Hence statement 2 is wrong.

**Q15. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - Article 32 is limited to enforcement of Fundamental Rights and is itself a Fundamental Right; Article 226 is wider as it covers both Fundamental Rights and 'any other purpose'. Article 32 can be suspended only during a National Emergency (except Articles 20 and 21). A High Court may issue writs beyond its territory if the cause of action arises within it.

**Q16. Answer: (b)** - *Hard* - Under Article 143(1) the Court may either give or refuse to give its opinion; under Article 143(2) (certain pre-Constitution treaties/agreements) it must give its opinion. In both cases the opinion is advisory and not binding on the President. Hence statement 1 is wrong.

**Q17. Answer: (d)** - *Easy* - Article 141 - law declared binding on all courts; Article 142 - complete justice; Article 137 - power of review; Article 129 - court of record. Correct: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

**Q18. Answer: (b)** - *Moderate* - The basic structure doctrine was laid down in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), holding that Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution. Minerva Mills (1980) later reinforced it; Golaknath (1967) had held Fundamental Rights unamendable, which Kesavananda modified.

**Q19. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - The 99th Amendment (2014) and the NJAC Act sought to replace the collegium system. In 2015, in the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association case, the Court struck them down as violative of the independence of the judiciary, a basic feature, restoring the collegium. Both statements are correct.

**Q20. Answer: (d)** - *Hard* - Vishaka - workplace sexual harassment guidelines; Vellore Citizens - precautionary principle and polluter pays; Hussainara Khatoon - right to speedy trial; Olga Tellis - right to livelihood. Correct: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

**Q21. Answer: (b)** - *Moderate* - The CACP (set up in 1965, originally as the Agricultural Prices Commission) is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and is only an advisory body - it is NOT statutory. It recommends MSPs, but the final decision rests with the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs. Statement 1 is wrong.

**Q22. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - MSP is announced for 23 crops - 7 cereals, 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds and 4 commercial crops (copra, raw cotton, raw jute and dehusked coconut/sugarcane category). Sugarcane is covered separately through the Fair and Remunerative Price.

**Q23. Answer: (a)** - *Hard* - A2 = actual paid-out costs; A2+FL = A2 plus imputed value of family labour; C2 is the comprehensive cost (A2+FL plus rent and interest on owned land and capital). The Swaminathan Committee recommended MSP at C2 plus 50%, whereas the government's announced formula is 1.5 times A2+FL. Hence statement 3 is wrong.

**Q24. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - The FRP for sugarcane is announced by the Central Government (approved by the CCEA) on the recommendation of the CACP under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966. Some states additionally declare a higher State Advised Price (SAP). Both statements are correct.

**Q25. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - The FCI was set up in 1965 under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, to undertake price support operations, procurement, storage, movement and distribution of foodgrains, and maintenance of buffer stocks.

**Q26. Answer: (d)** - *Moderate* - The NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population (about two-thirds of the country). Priority households get 5 kg per person per month, while AAY households continue to get 35 kg per household per month. All three statements are correct.

**Q27. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - e-NAM (National Agriculture Market), launched in April 2016, is an online trading platform linking APMC mandis to create a unified national market. The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, launched in 2020, is a Rs 1 lakh crore financing facility for post-harvest and farm-gate infrastructure. Both statements are correct.

**Q28. Answer: (d)** - *Hard* - Under PMFBY the farmer's premium share is capped at 2% for kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops; the balance is shared by the Centre and States. All three statements are correct.

**Q29. Answer: (d)** - *Easy* - PMKSY aims at 'Har Khet Ko Pani' and 'More Crop Per Drop'. Its components include the Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP), Har Khet Ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop, and the Watershed Development component. All three are correct.

**Q30. Answer: (d)** - *Easy* - The Cabinet Mission (March-June 1946) had three British Cabinet members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India), Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander. All three are correct.

**Q31. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - The Cabinet Mission rejected the demand for a separate sovereign Pakistan and instead proposed a three-tier arrangement of a weak Union, Groups (A, B, C) of provinces, and Provinces. It did not offer immediate Dominion status; it provided for a Constituent Assembly and an interim government. Statement 3 is wrong.

**Q32. Answer: (a)** - *Easy* - The Muslim League called for Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946 to press for Pakistan, leading to the 'Great Calcutta Killings' and widespread communal violence.

**Q33. Answer: (b)** - *Hard* - RIN Mutiny (February 1946) -> Interim Government (2 September 1946) -> first sitting of the Constituent Assembly (9 December 1946) -> Mountbatten (June Third) Plan (3 June 1947). Correct order: 1-2-3-4.

**Q34. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - The Mountbatten Plan provided for the partition of Bengal and Punjab (their assemblies voting in two halves) and a referendum in NWFP and Sylhet. The princely states were given the choice of acceding to India or Pakistan - independence was NOT offered as an option under the plan. Statement 2 is wrong.

**Q35. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - The Act abolished the office of the Secretary of State for India and ended Crown paramountcy over the princely states. It provided that each dominion would have its own Governor-General; it did not make a common Governor-General compulsory (Mountbatten served as common Governor-General only by mutual request). Statement 3 is wrong.

**Q36. Answer: (c)** - *Easy* - The Boundary Commissions for Bengal and Punjab were headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe; the demarcation is known as the Radcliffe Line, and the award was published shortly after independence.

**Q37. Answer: (d)** - *Hard* - Regulating Act 1773 - Governor-General of Bengal; Pitt's India Act 1784 - Board of Control and dual government; Charter Act 1833 - Governor-General of India and first Law Commission (Macaulay); Government of India Act 1858 - end of Company rule and Crown government. Correct: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

**Q38. Answer: (d)** - *Moderate* - The Morley-Minto Reforms (Act of 1909) introduced separate electorates; the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Act of 1919) introduced dyarchy in the provinces; and the Act of 1935 provided for a Federal Court (established 1937), provincial autonomy and the RBI. All three statements are correct.

**Q39. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - Rural-to-rural is the dominant migration stream in India, largely on account of marriage migration of women. Rural-to-urban migration is significant for economic reasons but is smaller in absolute numbers.

**Q40. Answer: (c)** - *Moderate* - Census data show that marriage is by far the leading reason for migration among women, whereas work and employment is the predominant reason for men. Both statements are correct.

**Q41. Answer: (b)** - *Moderate* - The demographic dividend is the economic growth potential that arises when the working-age population (15-59/64) is larger than the dependent (non-working) population, lowering the dependency ratio. India is currently in this window.

**Q42. Answer: (d)** - *Hard* - The HDI, published by UNDP in the Human Development Report since 1990, combines a long and healthy life (life expectancy), knowledge (education), and a decent standard of living (GNI per capita). It was conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with the collaboration of Amartya Sen. All three statements are correct.

**Q43. Answer: (a)** - *Easy* - In India, the sex ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males. (Some countries express it as males per 1000 females, but the Indian convention is females per 1000 males.)

**Q44. Answer: (a)** - *Easy* - Population density is the number of persons living per unit area (usually per square kilometre). It is a measure of the concentration of population, distinct from total population or growth rate.

**Q45. Answer: (b)** - *Easy* - The Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel) were enunciated in the 1954 Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Tibet region of China and India.

**Q46. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - Panchsheel Agreement (1954) -> Agreement on Maintenance of Peace and Tranquillity along the LAC (1993) -> Border Defence Cooperation Agreement (2013). Correct order: 3-1-2.

**Q47. Answer: (d)** - *Hard* - Aksai Chin, in the western sector, is under Chinese control but claimed by India. The Shaksgam Valley (Trans-Karakoram Tract) was ceded by Pakistan to China under the 1963 agreement. The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo. All three statements are correct.

**Q48. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - The October 2024 understanding related to Depsang and Demchok - the last two friction points - enabling disengagement and resumption of patrolling there. (Doklam lies in the Sikkim sector, not Ladakh.)

**Q49. Answer: (a)** - *Moderate* - Water Act (1974) -> Air Act (1981) -> Environment (Protection) Act (1986, the umbrella legislation enacted after the Bhopal disaster and in the spirit of the 1972 Stockholm Conference). Correct order: 1-2-3.

**Q50. Answer: (d)** - *Moderate* - The AQI (2014) covers eight pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3 and Pb) and has six categories - Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor and Severe. The overall index is set by the pollutant with the worst (highest) sub-index. All three statements are correct.

2. **DRSCs:** 24 committees, 31 members each (21 LS + 10 RS), 16 under Speaker + 8 under RS Chairman; recommendations advisory.
3. **IPG (1949)** is autonomous, NOT a parliamentary committee; **Parliamentary Forums** from 2005.
4. **SC strength now 38 (CJI + 37)** - Number of Judges Amendment Act 2026; Article 124 lets Parliament fix the number; no minimum age; distinguished-jurist route never used.
5. **Art 131 exclusive** but inter-State water disputes excluded via **Art 262**; **Art 143(1) may decline, 143(2) must answer**, opinion never binding.
6. **Basic structure = Kesavananda 1973**; NJAC + 99th Amendment struck down 2015; collegium restored.
7. **PIL map:** Vishaka (harassment), Vellore (precautionary + polluter pays), Hussainara Khatoon (speedy trial), Olga Tellis (livelihood).
8. **MSP cost concepts:** A2 -> A2+FL -> C2; government formula 1.5x A2+FL vs **Swaminathan C2+50%**; MSP for **23 crops**; CACP advisory (est. 1965), FCI under Act of 1964.
9. **NFSA 2013:** 75% rural / 50% urban; priority 5 kg/person/month; AAY 35 kg/household. **PMFBY:** 2% kharif / 1.5% rabi / 5% commercial.
10. **Partition chronology:** RIN Mutiny Feb 1946 -> Interim Govt 2 Sep 1946 -> Constituent Assembly 9 Dec 1946 -> Mountbatten Plan 3 Jun 1947 -> Independence Act assent 18 Jul 1947.
11. **Mountbatten Plan:** princely states could join India OR Pakistan - **independence was not an option**; Bengal & Punjab partitioned; NWFP/Sylhet referendum; Radcliffe drew the line.
12. **Constitutional ladder:** 1773 GG of Bengal, 1784 Board of Control, 1833 GG of India + first Law Commission, 1858 Crown rule, 1909 separate electorates, 1919 provincial dyarchy, 1935 Federal Court + provincial autonomy.
13. **Migration:** rural-to-rural largest; marriage = top reason for women, work for men. **Demographic dividend** = working-age > dependents.
14. **India-China ladder:** Panchsheel 1954 -> Peace & Tranquillity 1993 -> BDCA 2013; Aksai Chin (China-held, India-claimed), Shaksgam ceded by Pakistan 1963, Brahmaputra = Yarlung Tsangpo; **Oct 2024 = Depsang & Demchok**.
15. **Pollution stack:** Water Act 1974 -> Air Act 1981 -> EPA 1986 (umbrella); **AQI 2014 = 8 pollutants, 6 categories, worst sub-index sets the index**.
